parts.title: The Benefits of Regular Physical Exercise
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Regular physical exercise is one of the simplest ways to stay healthy. Doctors around the world recommend that adults do at least thirty minutes of moderate activity on most days of the week, and that children be even more active. Modern life makes it easy to avoid movement, because lifts, cars, and online shopping save time and effort. Despite this advice, many people spend most of their day sitting at a desk, in a car, or in front of a screen, and they rarely think about the long-term effects on their bodies.

Exercise brings many clear benefits to the human body. It strengthens the heart and lungs, helps to control weight, and lowers the risk of serious illness. People who walk, swim, or cycle regularly also build stronger muscles and bones, which makes everyday tasks such as carrying shopping or climbing stairs much easier as they grow older. In addition, exercise can **boost** energy levels, so active people often feel less tired after work than people who rarely move. Even gentle activities such as gardening or dancing at home count as exercise. Doctors also link exercise to better sleep and a stronger immune system.

Physical activity is also good for the mind. When we exercise, the body releases chemicals that improve our mood and reduce stress, which is why a short walk can make a bad day feel better. Many students find that they concentrate more easily after sport, and research suggests that regular exercise may help older adults to keep their memory sharp. Exercising outdoors in fresh air can make people feel calmer and more relaxed. Exercise also helps people to **maintain** a positive attitude when they face problems at work or at school.

Exercise is often a social activity as well. Joining a football team, a dance class, or a walking group allows people to meet new friends and share their interests. Exercising with a partner can make the time pass more quickly and keep both people motivated. However, some people avoid sport because they think gyms are expensive or embarrassing places. Fortunately, there are many free options, such as jogging in a park or doing simple exercises at home, and most of **them** require no special equipment.

In conclusion, regular exercise improves both physical and mental health, and it does not need to be difficult or expensive. Experts suggest that beginners should start slowly, choose activities they enjoy, and increase the time gradually, so that exercise becomes a natural part of the week rather than a painful duty. Setting small goals, such as walking ten thousand steps a day or climbing the stairs instead of taking the lift, can help people to stay motivated. Remember that the best exercise is the one that you will actually do. With a little patience, almost anyone can develop a healthy habit that will bring benefits for many years.

parts.title: The Evolution of E-Learning in Modern Education
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Learning from a distance is not a new idea, though its methods have changed. In the nineteenth century, correspondence courses delivered by post allowed students in remote areas to study without attending a school, and radio and television later extended this principle to much larger audiences. Early distance courses were slow and isolating, because feedback could take weeks to arrive. What has changed in recent decades is the speed, scale, and interactivity of the technology, which has turned e-learning from a niche alternative into a central part of mainstream education.

The arrival of the internet brought the first truly major change in this field. In the 1990s, universities began to place lecture notes and discussion forums online, and learning management systems soon allowed teachers to distribute materials, set assignments, and track progress from a single platform. Many universities now record lectures so that students can review them. The next milestone came in 2012, when several American universities launched massive open online courses, or MOOCs, which attracted learners from around the world.

The pandemic of 2020 accelerated the adoption of online learning around the world. Within weeks, schools and universities in more than a hundred countries closed their buildings, and teachers who had never taught online were suddenly required to deliver lessons through video platforms. The experience was uneven: some institutions adapted quickly and creatively, while others struggled with poor connections, unfamiliar software, and students who found it hard to stay engaged in front of a screen. Nevertheless, the emergency forced education systems to confront questions about technology that they had postponed for years.

Supporters of e-learning emphasise its flexibility and its potential to personalise instruction. Students can study at their own pace, revisit difficult lectures, and fit education around work or family responsibilities, advantages that are particularly valuable for adult learners. Adaptive software can also analyse a learner's mistakes and offer tailored exercises, and virtual simulations let medical or engineering students practise procedures that would be dangerous or expensive to perform in reality. Properly designed, technology can **augment** the work of teachers rather than replace it.

Critics, however, point to several persistent problems that technology alone cannot solve. Access to reliable internet and suitable devices remains deeply unequal, so the shift online risks widening existing educational **disparities** between wealthy and poor households, and between urban and rural communities. Completion rates in open courses are often low, because learners who lack structure and personal contact find it difficult to remain motivated. Moreover, some skills, including teamwork, laboratory technique, and the social development that occurs in classrooms, are hard to cultivate through a screen, and **those** who study entirely alone may miss them.

Most educators now expect blended learning, which combines online resources with face-to-face teaching, to become the dominant model. Artificial intelligence is likely to play a growing role, offering instant feedback and personalised support, but it also raises concerns about privacy, cheating, and the quality of automatically generated material. Teacher training is therefore as important as the platforms themselves. Ultimately, the success of e-learning will depend less on the sophistication of the technology than on how thoughtfully teachers and institutions use it to serve students' needs.

parts.title: The Emergence of the Subscription Economy
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: A generation ago, most consumers bought products outright: a newspaper from a kiosk, a film on a disc, software in a box. Today, many of those purchases have been replaced by recurring payments that grant access rather than ownership. Music, television, cloud storage, razors, meal kits, and even car features are now sold by subscription, and analysts describe the shift as the rise of the subscription economy.

The underlying idea of paying regularly for ongoing access is by no means new. Newspapers and magazines have been delivered to subscribers for centuries, and utilities such as electricity and water have long billed households at regular intervals. What is new is the application of this model to almost every category of consumer goods and services, made possible by cheap digital delivery, widespread broadband, and payment systems that can bill customers automatically.

For companies, the main appeal of subscriptions is the predictability of their income. A one-off sale produces revenue once, whereas a subscriber who stays for years generates a steady stream of income that investors can forecast with confidence. **[1]** This stability allows firms to plan product development, hire staff, and borrow money more cheaply than businesses whose sales fluctuate. **[2]** Subscriptions also generate detailed data about how customers use a service, which can be used to refine offerings and to suggest further purchases. **[3]** Many investors now value such companies on the basis of recurring revenue rather than annual profit. **[4]**

For consumers, the attraction is convenience, flexibility, and a much lower upfront cost. Paying a modest monthly fee for thousands of films or songs is cheaper than buying them individually, and cancelling is, in theory, easy. In practice, however, many companies rely on **inertia**: customers who sign up for a free trial often forget to cancel, or find the process deliberately tedious, so they continue paying for services they rarely use. Surveys in several countries suggest that the average household underestimates its monthly subscription spending by a considerable margin.

The subscription model has also reshaped the way that businesses compete with each other. Older firms that once sold software licences or physical media have moved to subscription, partly to protect revenue against piracy and partly to keep customers inside their own ecosystems. Meanwhile, start-ups have used subscriptions to challenge incumbent companies in sectors as varied as razors, mattresses, and fitness equipment. However, markets in which a handful of dominant platforms bundle many services together can make it difficult for smaller rivals to attract and retain subscribers.

Regulators in several countries have begun to respond to the growing volume of complaints. Several jurisdictions now require companies to disclose renewal terms clearly, send reminders before free trials end, and allow cancellation through the same channel used to sign up. Consumer groups argue that **these** measures are overdue, since so-called dark patterns, which are interface designs that nudge users towards costly choices, have become widespread. Industry representatives counter that excessive regulation could stifle innovation and raise prices for the very customers it aims to protect.

The subscription economy is therefore neither a passing fashion nor an unqualified benefit. It has made many goods more accessible and given businesses stable foundations, yet it can also encourage waste, hidden costs, and a feeling that ownership of anything has become impossible. Whether it becomes a fair partnership between firms and customers will depend on transparent pricing, genuine choice, and the willingness of consumers to review what they pay for.

parts.title: The Great Deep-Sea Mining Debate
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Scattered across the abyssal plains of the Pacific Ocean, at depths of four to six kilometres, lie vast numbers of potato-sized lumps of rock known as polymetallic nodules. They contain nickel, cobalt, copper, and manganese, metals central to modern batteries and wind turbines. As land-based deposits become harder to find and more costly to exploit, a growing number of companies and governments have started to look to the seabed.

The legal framework that governs this activity is unusual by any standard. Under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, the seabed beyond national jurisdiction is designated the common heritage of humankind, and the International Seabed Authority regulates activity there. Dozens of exploration contracts have been granted, yet detailed rules for commercial extraction have still not been agreed.

Advocates make a case for seabed mining that genuinely deserves serious consideration. Producing the same metals on land often requires clearing forests, displacing communities, and, in some regions, relying on hazardous or exploitative labour. Nodules, by contrast, lie loose on the seafloor, so extraction would not involve digging open pits or generating the large volumes of waste rock associated with conventional mines. Supporters also note that demand for battery metals is projected to rise sharply as electric vehicles spread, and they argue that a secure, diversified supply is essential to meeting climate targets.

Opponents respond that the deep ocean is among the least understood environments on Earth. Scientists have described thousands of species on the nodule fields, the majority of them previously unknown, and many appear to live nowhere else. **[1]** Removing nodules would destroy the hard surfaces on which some animals attach themselves, and a creature that has evolved over millions of years in stable darkness cannot easily adapt to sudden change. **[2]** Mining machines would also stir up clouds of sediment that could drift for considerable distances before settling, potentially smothering filter-feeding organisms far from the extraction site. **[3]** Noise and light pollution add further stress to an ecosystem that has existed without either. **[4]**

Nodules accumulate extremely slowly, growing by only a few millimetres over a million years, and **this** means that any mined area would be effectively unrecoverable on human timescales. Many biologists therefore fear that the damage would be **irreversible** in practice. They warn that the scale of the unknowns is itself a reason for restraint. Because most of the species living on the nodule fields have not yet been formally described, it is currently impossible to predict which organisms would be lost or whether ecosystems could recover.

In response, a number of governments, scientific bodies, and major technology companies have called for a **moratorium** until the risks are better understood, and several have pledged not to use seabed minerals. Supporters of mining counter that research cannot be completed without commercial-scale trials, and that a ban would simply push demand towards land-based sources whose environmental and human costs are already well documented. The disagreement has also exposed tensions within the International Seabed Authority, whose dual mandate requires it both to promote mineral development and to protect the marine environment. No agreement has yet emerged on how to resolve this dilemma among the member states.

The deep-sea mining debate therefore pits two urgent goals against each other: securing the minerals needed to decarbonise economies, and preserving ecosystems that humanity has barely begun to explore. Recycling, improved battery chemistries, and reduced demand could ease the pressure, though few experts believe they can eliminate it entirely. What happens next will show how institutions balance short-term ambition against long-term responsibility for the global commons.

tasks.guide_md:
**1. Phân tích đề bài và xác định dạng đề:**
- Đây là dạng thư thân mật (Informal Email) gửi cho bạn bè.
- Người viết cần trả lời 3 câu hỏi: Gợi ý hoạt động, xác nhận sở thích ăn socola của bố mẹ và hướng dẫn cách di chuyển từ sân bay.
- Đảm bảo độ dài tối thiểu 120 từ và sử dụng ngôn từ tự nhiên, gần gũi.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục logic (Organization):**
- Greeting: Chào hỏi thân mật như 'Hi Mark,' hoặc 'Dear Mark,'.
- Opening: Bày tỏ sự hào hứng trước chuyến thăm của bạn. Ví dụ: 'I am thrilled to hear that you are coming to visit me next month!'
- Body Paragraph 1: Gợi ý các hoạt động như đi tham quan, ăn uống. Ví dụ: 'We should definitely try some local street food and visit the city museum.'
- Body Paragraph 2: Trả lời về món quà socola. Ví dụ: 'Regarding the gift, my parents actually love dark chocolate, so that would be perfect!'
- Body Paragraph 3: Hướng dẫn đường đi. Ví dụ: 'The most convenient way to get to my house is by taking a taxi or a ride-sharing app like Grab.'
- Closing: Kết thúc thư và mong sớm gặp lại. Ví dụ: 'I can't wait to see you. Safe travels!'
- Sign-off: 'Best wishes,' hoặc 'Cheers,'.

**3. Chiến lược đạt điểm cao (Vocabulary & Grammar):**
- Sử dụng thì tương lai (Will/Be going to) cho các dự định và thì hiện tại đơn cho sở thích.
- Sử dụng các cấu trúc gợi ý như 'How about...?', 'I suggest...', 'It would be great if...'.

Questions:

Let’s talk about money

1
Do you use money often in your daily life?
2

parts.guide_md:
**1. Phân tích đề bài:**
- Part 1 gồm 6 câu hỏi cá nhân trong khoảng 3 phút. Bạn cần trả lời nhanh, tự nhiên và có giải thích ngắn gọn.
- **Topic A (Money):** Câu hỏi 1–3 tập trung vào việc sử dụng tiền, giáo dục tài chính cho trẻ em và trải nghiệm mua món đồ đắt tiền nhất.
- **Topic B (Food):** Câu hỏi 4–6 nói về thói quen ăn sáng, chế độ ăn uống và quan điểm về lối sống lành mạnh.
- Giám khảo đánh giá khả năng phản xạ giao tiếp, độ lưu loát, từ vựng và phát âm.
- Nên chia thời gian đều cho cả hai chủ đề, khoảng 25–35 giây cho mỗi câu hỏi.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục khi nói (Organization):**
- Sử dụng công thức ARE: Answer -> Reason -> Example để mở rộng ý.
- **Ví dụ Topic A:** Yes, I use money every day because I need to pay for food, transportation and study materials. For example, I usually buy coffee and lunch near my university.
- **Ví dụ Topic B:** I usually have bread and milk for breakfast because they are quick and convenient in the morning.
- Luôn tự hỏi Why? hoặc How? để kéo dài câu trả lời tự nhiên hơn.
- Khi chuyển chủ đề, bạn có thể nói: Besides managing money, I also pay attention to my eating habits and health.

**3. Chiến lược đạt điểm cao (Fluency, Vocabulary & Grammar):**
- Duy trì tốc độ nói ổn định, tránh nói quá nhanh hoặc dừng lại quá lâu.
- Với Topic A, nên dùng hiện tại đơn để mô tả thói quen và hiện tại hoàn thành khi nói về món đồ đắt nhất từng mua.
- Với Topic B, dùng trạng từ tần suất như usually, often, rarely để nói về chế độ ăn uống.
- Nếu quên từ vựng, hãy diễn đạt bằng cách đơn giản hơn thay vì im lặng.
- Từ vựng Topic A: save money (tiết kiệm tiền), financial responsibility (trách nhiệm tài chính), spend wisely (chi tiêu hợp lý), budget management (quản lý ngân sách).
- Từ vựng Topic B: balanced diet (chế độ ăn cân bằng), nutritious food (thực phẩm bổ dưỡng), healthy habits (thói quen lành mạnh), fast food consumption (việc ăn đồ ăn nhanh).
Cụm từ quan trọng nên dùng:
- learn how to manage personal finances – học cách quản lý tài chính cá nhân
- avoid wasting money on unnecessary things – tránh lãng phí tiền vào những thứ không cần thiết
- save up for expensive purchases – tiết kiệm để mua món đồ đắt tiền
- have a nutritious breakfast every morning – ăn sáng đầy đủ dinh dưỡng mỗi sáng
- maintain a balanced lifestyle – duy trì lối sống cân bằng
- exercise regularly and eat healthy food – tập thể dục thường xuyên và ăn uống lành mạnh
Từ nối khi nói (Linking Words):
- First of all – trước hết
- Besides that – bên cạnh đó
- For instance – ví dụ
- However – tuy nhiên
- As a result – kết quả là
Cách thể hiện quan điểm tự nhiên:
- Personally, I think children should learn about money at an early age. – Cá nhân tôi nghĩ trẻ em nên học về tiền từ sớm.
- In my opinion, spending money wisely is an important life skill. – Theo tôi, chi tiêu hợp lý là kỹ năng sống quan trọng.
- I would say my laptop is the most expensive thing I have ever bought. – Tôi cho rằng laptop là món đồ đắt nhất tôi từng mua.
- To be honest, I sometimes skip breakfast because I wake up late. – Thành thật mà nói đôi khi tôi bỏ bữa sáng vì thức dậy muộn.
- From my perspective, a healthy lifestyle includes both exercise and good eating habits. – Theo quan điểm của tôi, lối sống lành mạnh bao gồm tập thể dục và ăn uống tốt.
- I believe eating too much fast food can negatively affect our health. – Tôi tin rằng ăn quá nhiều đồ ăn nhanh có thể ảnh hưởng xấu đến sức khỏe.

**4. Các lỗi thường gặp:**
- Chỉ trả lời Yes hoặc No mà không giải thích thêm là lỗi rất phổ biến.
- Ở Topic A, nhiều bạn chỉ nói thích mua đồ mà không giải thích lý do hoặc trải nghiệm cá nhân.
- Ở Topic B, nhiều bạn lặp lại từ healthy quá nhiều thay vì dùng balanced hoặc nutritious.
- Dùng sai thì khi nói về trải nghiệm mua món đồ đắt nhất.

**5. Chiến lược xử lý khi bí ý hoặc quên từ:**
- Có thể dùng câu filler như: That is an interesting question, let me think for a moment.
- Nếu quên từ vựng, hãy mô tả chức năng hoặc ví dụ thay thế.
- Ở Topic A, nếu quên tên món đồ đắt tiền, hãy mô tả công dụng của nó.
- Ở Topic B, nếu quên tên món ăn bằng tiếng Anh, hãy mô tả thành phần chính của món ăn.

**6. Tư duy làm bài nói:**
- Hãy coi đây là một cuộc trò chuyện tự nhiên thay vì cố học thuộc câu trả lời.
- Khi chuyển từ chủ đề tiền bạc sang sức khỏe, hãy thay đổi ý tưởng rõ ràng để tránh bị lặp.
- Sự lưu loát và tự tin quan trọng hơn việc dùng quá nhiều từ vựng phức tạp.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục khi nói (Organization):**
- Sử dụng cấu trúc State opinion -> Give reasons -> Compare -> Conclude để trình bày rõ ràng.

- Nếu quên từ vựng, hãy paraphrase bằng các cụm đơn giản hơn như big celebration hoặc private event.
Cụm từ quan trọng nên dùng:
- create unforgettable memories – tạo ra những kỷ niệm khó quên

- cost a significant amount of money – tốn khá nhiều tiền

- Thời gian khoảng 5 phút, nên dành khoảng 3 phút cho bài nói chính và phần còn lại cho hỏi đáp.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục khi nói (Organization):**
- Sử dụng cấu trúc FEEL: Point -> Explanation -> Example -> Link để triển khai từng ý trong mindmap.
- **Ví dụ 1:** Today, I would like to talk about several important factors people should consider when choosing a job.
- **Ví dụ 2:** Another important factor is work-life balance because employees need time for family and relaxation.
- Hãy đưa ví dụ thực tế như kinh nghiệm làm part-time hoặc quan sát từ người thân.
- Luôn đi theo thứ tự của mindmap để tránh lặp ý và giữ bài nói logic.

**3. Chiến lược đạt điểm cao (Fluency, Vocabulary & Grammar):**
- Sử dụng câu chuyển ý như Moving on to the next factor hoặc Another thing worth mentioning is.
- Dùng hiện tại đơn để nói sự thật chung và hiện tại hoàn thành khi nói về thay đổi trong thị trường lao động.
- Có thể paraphrase job bằng career, occupation hoặc profession.
Cụm từ quan trọng nên dùng:
- competitive salary and attractive benefits – mức lương cạnh tranh và phúc lợi hấp dẫn
- positive working environment – môi trường làm việc tích cực
- opportunities for professional development – cơ hội phát triển nghề nghiệp
- achieve a healthy work-life balance – đạt được cân bằng giữa công việc và cuộc sống
- gain valuable working experience – tích lũy kinh nghiệm làm việc quý giá
- long-term career prospects – triển vọng nghề nghiệp lâu dài
Từ nối khi nói (Linking Words):
- First of all – trước hết
- In addition – thêm vào đó
- For example – ví dụ
- As a result – kết quả là
- Finally – cuối cùng
Cách thể hiện quan điểm tự nhiên:
- In my opinion, salary is important but it should not be the only factor. – Theo tôi, lương quan trọng nhưng không nên là yếu tố duy nhất.
- I personally prefer a friendly working environment because it reduces stress. – Cá nhân tôi thích môi trường làm việc thân thiện vì nó giúp giảm áp lực.
- From my perspective, young people should choose jobs that help them grow professionally. – Theo quan điểm của tôi, người trẻ nên chọn công việc giúp họ phát triển nghề nghiệp.

opportunities and stability.
